title: Java: which APIs and framework defaults turn into vulnerabilities?
short: Never let outside data name the class it becomes, keep input out of queries and expressions, and move off Spring Boot 3.5, without free fixes since June 2026.
answer: Before your next release, move to JDK 25 or 21 and Spring Boot 4.1[^sbsupport], stop deserializing outside data into classes it names, and require Find Security Bugs or CodeQL in CI. Judge everything else by whether outside data can pick a class, become SQL, an expression or a command, reach an XML parser, a path or a URL, or slip past an authorization rule.
audience: Developers and tech leads writing production Java, including Spring Boot services, and the security people who review it

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Stay on supported lines and patch quarterly.
items.text: OpenJDK ships fixes every January, April, July and October[^ojvuln]. Spring Boot 3.5 lost free fixes in June 2026, 4.0 loses them in December and 4.1 in July 2027[^sbsupport]. Patch within the patching sheet's deadlines.

items.title: Never let outside data name the class.
items.text: Java deserialization creates the classes the stream names, and no filter runs unless you set one[^serfilter]; Jackson's default typing lets JSON do the same[^jackson]. Read outside data as JSON into records.

items.title: Keep input out of queries, expressions and commands.
items.text: Use parameters for SQL and JPQL, never parse SpEL or OGNL from input, and give `ProcessBuilder` an argument list. SQL, OS command and code injection rank 2nd, 9th and 10th in the CWE Top 25[^cwe].

items.title: Deny by default and keep actuator private.
items.text: End your rules with `.anyRequest().denyAll()`[^ssauthz] and expose only `health`, Boot's default[^actuator]. ActiveMQ's Jolokia endpoint let logged-in users run code (CVE-2026-34197, exploited)[^amq][^kev].

items.title: Make the analyzers a required check.
items.text: Run Find Security Bugs or CodeQL on every pull request[^fsb][^cql]. Set Dependency-Check's `failBuildOnCVSS`: by default it never fails[^odc].

items.title: Where does outside data enter?
items.text: Find the controllers, listeners, uploads and batch jobs it touches. Each should bind a record made for that request, as Spring advises[^modelattr], not an entity: Spring4Shell was code execution through data binding[^kev].

items.title: Who may call it, on which record?
items.text: Ask why for each new `permitAll()`, each matcher placed after a broader one[^ssauthz] and each `csrf` change. Missing authorization ranks 4th in the CWE Top 25[^cwe]: check who owns the record.

items.title: Can data choose a class or code?
Does it reach SQL, a process, XML, a path or a URL?
items.text: Check `createQuery` and `@Query` strings built with `+`, `ProcessBuilder`, XML parser factories, `resolve(` and HTTP clients given URLs from input.

items.title: What does it expose?
items.text: Check `exposure.include`, new `SecurityFilterChain` beans, which replace Boot's actuator rules[^actuator], error details and logged secrets.

blocks.title: Java traps and what to use instead
items: **`ObjectInputStream.readObject()` and `XMLDecoder`.** The stream picks the classes, and gadgets on the classpath turn that into code execution[^serfilter]; OWASP lists `XMLDecoder` as unsafe for untrusted input[^owaspdeser]. If you must read Java serialization, set `jdk.serialFilter` to an allowlist ending in `!*`, with `maxbytes` and `maxdepth` limits[^serpattern].

**`activateDefaultTyping()` and `@JsonTypeInfo(use = Id.CLASS)`.** The JSON then names the class, and Jackson calls the validator you pass critical for security[^jackson]. Use `Id.NAME` with listed subtypes[^fsb]. XStream with a relaxed allowlist, SnakeYAML without `SafeConstructor` and fastjson without safe mode share the problem[^owaspdeser].

**`DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance()` defaults.** JDK parsers fetch external DTDs and entities unless you set secure processing explicitly[^jaxp], and GeoServer's XXE (CVE-2025-58360) is exploited[^kev]. Set `jdk.xml.dtd.support=deny` on JDK 25, or the `disallow-doctype-decl` feature for DOM and SAX and `SUPPORT_DTD` false for StAX[^jaxp].

**`"WHERE id = " + id` in JDBC, JPQL or a native `@Query`.** Hibernate queries are injectable when you concatenate[^owaspsqli]. Bind `?` or `:name` parameters, and map sort columns and directions from a fixed list: parameters can't stand for column names[^owaspsqli].

**SpEL, OGNL, `Class.forName()` or JNDI `lookup()` fed from input.** Spring says `StandardEvaluationContext` must never evaluate untrusted SpEL and `SimpleEvaluationContext` is only best-effort[^spel]. Exploited flaws in Spring Cloud Function (SpEL), Confluence (OGNL) and PaperCut (reflection) are on CISA's list[^kev]; Log4Shell ran LDAP code named in a log message[^log4j]. Keep input in variables and map names from a fixed list.

**`Runtime.exec(String)` and `sh -c`.** `exec(String)` splits on whitespace and is deprecated since JDK 18[^runtime]. Give `ProcessBuilder` a fixed program and one element per argument, put `--` before input that may start with a dash, and never hand input to `sh -c` or `cmd /c`.

**`base.resolve(name)`.** An absolute `name` replaces `base`, and `normalize()` ignores symlinks[^path]. Require `startsWith(base)` on the normalized path, which compares whole name elements, and on `toRealPath()` where links matter[^path]. Check `ZipEntry` names too.

**`new URL(input).openStream()` and HTTP clients given URLs from input.** URL connections also open `file:` URLs[^fsb], and server-side request forgery ranks 22nd in the CWE Top 25[^cwe]. Allowlist hosts, check the resolved address and keep `HttpClient`'s default of no redirects[^httpclient].

blocks.title: Tools that catch it
items: **Find Security Bugs.** Add `findsecbugs-plugin` to SpotBugs and fix `OBJECT_DESERIALIZATION`, `XXE_DOCUMENT`, `SQL_INJECTION_JPA` and `SPEL_INJECTION` first[^fsb].
**Error Prone** flags `BanJNDI` as an error by default; turn on the experimental `BanSerializableRead` and `BanClassLoader` checks[^ep].
**CodeQL**'s `java/unsafe-deserialization`, `java/xxe` and `java/jndi-injection` queries cover these traps[^cql].
**Dependency-Check** fails builds only once you set `failBuildOnCVSS`[^odc]. The supply-chain sheet covers the rest.

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **The Security Manager.** JDK 24 disabled it for good, and servers rarely used it[^jep486]. Isolate untrusted code in a process or container.
**Hunting gadget classes.** OWASP expects more to be found[^owaspdeser]. Stop deserializing outside data instead.
**Find Security Bugs' inventory patterns.** `SPRING_ENDPOINT` and `SERVLET_PARAMETER` flag every controller and parameter read[^fsb]. Exclude them.
**Escaping input for SQL, shells or SpEL yourself.** Bind parameters, drop the shell and stop evaluating input instead.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **Oracle JDK 21 updates are no longer no-fee.** Releases since 20 October 2026 use the OTN license; Oracle JDK 25 updates stay no-fee until September 2028[^oracle]. Temurin supports 21 until at least December 2029[^temurin].

**Compromised eMudhra CA keys need another JDK update.** Install a runtime that fixes JDK-8395690 (CVE-2026-114820) in every image, even if you updated in October; on Debian and Ubuntu, also rebuild the Java keystore[^ojemudhra].
**Spring Boot 4.0.0 to 4.0.5 could leave every endpoint open** in some apps relying on Boot's default web security (CVE-2026-40976, critical)[^sp40976].
**Free Spring fixes now skip Spring Security 6.5.** August's critical fix for its embedded LDAP server (CVE-2026-59270) shipped free only for 7.0 and 7.1[^sp59270].

blocks.title: What this looks like for your code

columns.title: New project
items: Start on JDK 25 and Spring Boot 4.1, with `.anyRequest().denyAll()` as the last rule.
Set `jdk.serialFilter=!*` and `jdk.xml.dtd.support=deny` if nothing needs serialization or DTDs.
Bind every request to a record and keep entities out of controllers.

columns.title: Existing codebase
items: Move Oracle JDK 21 to JDK 25 or an OpenJDK build, and leave JDK 11 and 17 before October 2027[^temurin].
Search for `ObjectInputStream`, `activateDefaultTyping`, `parseExpression` and `exposure.include`.
Remove Log4j 1, at end of life since 2015[^log4j].

columns.title: High-assurance or regulated
items: Make CodeQL's `security-extended` suite and Find Security Bugs required checks.
Run with an allowlist `jdk.serialFilter` and the strict JAXP template as the JAXP configuration file[^jaxp].
Stay on Spring and JDK lines with free fixes, or pay for support on the ones you keep.
